title: "Two sides of decomposition: separability and divisibility"
date: "2025-02-23 08:42:00 +01:00"
draft: true
---

 

Decomposition, factorisation, division, separation, similar but not the same.

Take any number, say 90, and work out its prime factors: $2 \times 3^2 \times 5$. Most of us learnt that any number can be _factored_ in this way. Factorisation is a kind of decomposition.

If you go on to study some mechanics then you'll learn that speed of a ball rolling down a slope can be separated into horizontal and vertical components and each can be calculated independently. Separability is another kind od decomposition.

The first thing you learn when studying electronics is the composition laws for resistors. In serial the resistances simply sum: $R = R_1 + R_2 + ... + R_n$. In parallel the rule is more complicated: $\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2} + ... + \frac{1}{R_n}$
